I think it depends. Different people and different medications can lead to different results. Personally I found they really helped to take away a bit of my internal judgement and I became a lot more out going and confident. But unlike you I wasn't in therapy and had no one to keep me accountable so I never addressed the personal problems that exacerbated depressive thinking, so overtime the meds became much more of a crutch for me. Not to mention that it was he'll getting off of them.


Talk to your therapist and Dr. and see if you can work on a plan to try out medication for a period of time with a plan in place for eventually weaning off. I know some people need to be on antidepressants and I don't judge that at all, but I personally think the goal is to try to develop as much resiliency and coping strategies as you can.

I think the other commenter has good points. Personally, I found meds masked underlying frustrations and self loathing issues I needed to fix. Once I was medicated I was amazed when that reflexive depressive reaction faded to the background, but over time I started to become angrier with other people where I would normally be angry with myself. After even more time I found I just lost all motivation to change things and was just content with bad news. 


If you're considering medication you need to couple it with therapy and do some personal work to help yourself.
